title: Payout Methods Hold Periods Schedule
content:
Four kinds of hold can stop transfers on Payout Methods: a new-method hold, a default-change security hold, a risk-review hold and an account-suspension hold. Their periods and reach are set per rail as follows.

## Periods that differ by rail

| Rail | New-method hold (calendar days after verification during which transfers to the new method are held) |
|---|---|
| Direct Deposit (ACH) | 5 |
| Fast Pay Debit Card | 3 |
| PayPal | 3 |
| Payoneer | 5 |
| International Wire Transfer | 10 |
| Western Union Cash Pickup | 10 |

## Periods and reach that are the same on every rail

| Hold | Every rail |
|---|---|
| Default-change security hold | 72 elapsed hours after the default method is changed, during which transfers to the new default are held |
| Risk-review hold | 5 business days before release |
| Account-suspension hold: transfers it stops | Every transfer on every payout method of the host account |
| Account-suspension hold: when it is released | On the day the host account is reinstated |

## Points of reference

- The new-method hold is counted in **calendar days** from verification; the default-change hold in **elapsed hours** from the moment the new default was set; the risk-review hold in **business days**.
- The account-suspension hold is the only hold whose reach is the whole host account rather than one method.

**Hypothetical reading.** An imagined Western Union Cash Pickup method carries a new-method hold of 10 calendar days after its verification, against 3 calendar days for an imagined PayPal method; a change of default on either rail carries the same 72-hour security hold.
